name: Question 17
problem:
The vector-valued function $f(\theta ,ϕ),$ given by

$$
f(\theta ,ϕ)=⟨3\operatorname{cosh}⁡ϕ,\,4\operatorname{sinh}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,\text{_____}⟩
$$

parametrizes one sheet of the hyperboloid of two sheets defined in Cartesian coordinates as 

$$
-\frac{{x}^{2}}{9}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{16}+\frac{{z}^{2}}{4}=-1.
$$

 

By first considering the transformations

$$
x=3Z,\,y=4Y,\,z=2X
$$

and writing the resulting system in cylindrical polar coordinates, determine the third component of $f.$

*Hint: You may use the fact that the hyperbola ${Z}^{2}-{r}^{2}={k}^{2}$ can be parametrized as $⟨Z,r⟩=⟨k\operatorname{cosh}⁡ϕ,\,k\operatorname{sinh}⁡ϕ⟩$* for $ϕ\in R.$
worked_solution:
First, substituting the transformations

$$
x=3Z,\,y=4Y,\,z=2X
$$

into our equation, we get

$$
{X}^{2}+{Y}^{2}-{Z}^{2}=-1.
$$

If $(r,\theta ,Z)$ are the cylindrical coordinates of a point and $(X,Y,Z)$ are the corresponding Cartesian coordinates of that point, then we have

$$
X=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,Y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,Z=Z.
$$

Substituting this into our equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{X}^{2}+{Y}^{2}-{Z}^{2} & =-1 \\ (r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2}+(r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )^{2}-{Z}^{2} & =-1 \\ {r}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )-{Z}^{2} & =-1 \\ {r}^{2}-{Z}^{2} & =-1 \\ {Z}^{2}-{r}^{2} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Here, the hyperbola ${Z}^{2}-{r}^{2}=1$ represents the intersection of our hyperboloid with the plane that passes through the $Z$-axis and makes the angle of $\theta $ with the positive $X$-axis. Using the hint, a parametrization of such hyperbola can be given as

$$
⟨Z,r⟩=⟨\operatorname{cosh}⁡ϕ,\,\operatorname{sinh}⁡ϕ⟩,\,ϕ\in R.
$$

Now, for any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(\theta ,ϕ) & =⟨x,y,z⟩ \\  & =⟨3Z,4Y,2X⟩ \\  & =⟨3Z,\,4r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,2r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ⟩ \\  & =⟨3\operatorname{cosh}⁡ϕ,\,4(\operatorname{sinh}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,2(\operatorname{sinh}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ⟩ \\  & =⟨3\operatorname{cosh}⁡ϕ,\,4\operatorname{sinh}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,2\operatorname{sinh}⁡ϕ\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $\theta \in [0,2\pi )$ and $ϕ\in R.$

Therefore, the third component of $f$ is $2\operatorname{sinh}⁡ϕ\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta .$

Question 17
?

The vector-valued function f(θ,ϕ), given by

f(θ,ϕ)=⟨3cosh⁡ϕ,4sinh⁡ϕsin⁡θ,_____⟩

parametrizes one sheet of the hyperboloid of two sheets defined in Cartesian coordinates as −x29+y216+z24=−1.

By first considering the transformations x=3Z,y=4Y,z=2X and writing the resulting system in cylindrical polar coordinates, determine the third component of f.

Hint: You may use the fact that the hyperbola Z2−r2=k2 can be parametrized as ⟨Z,r⟩=⟨kcosh⁡ϕ,ksinh⁡ϕ⟩ for ϕ∈R.

a
2sinh⁡ϕsin⁡θ
b
2cosh⁡ϕcos⁡θ
c
4sinh⁡ϕ
d
4cos⁡θ
e
2sinh⁡ϕcos⁡θ
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, substituting the transformations x=3Z,y=4Y,z=2X into our equation, we get X2+Y2−Z2=−1.

If (r,θ,Z) are the cylindrical coordinates of a point and (X,Y,Z) are the corresponding Cartesian coordinates of that point, then we have X=rcos⁡θ,Y=rsin⁡θ,Z=Z.

Substituting this into our equation, we get X2+Y2−Z2=−1(rcos⁡θ)2+(rsin⁡θ)2−Z2=−1r2(cos2⁡θ+sin2⁡θ)−Z2=−1r2−Z2=−1Z2−r2=1.

Here, the hyperbola Z2−r2=1 represents the intersection of our hyperboloid with the plane that passes through the Z-axis and makes the angle of θ with the positive X-axis. Using the hint, a parametrization of such hyperbola can be given as ⟨Z,r⟩=⟨cosh⁡ϕ,sinh⁡ϕ⟩,ϕ∈R.

Now, for any point (x,y,z) on our surface, we obtain the following: f(θ,ϕ)=⟨x,y,z⟩=⟨3Z,4Y,2X⟩=⟨3Z,4rsin⁡θ,2rcos⁡θ⟩=⟨3cosh⁡ϕ,4(sinh⁡ϕ)sin⁡θ,2(sinh⁡ϕ)cos⁡θ⟩=⟨3cosh⁡ϕ,4sinh⁡ϕsin⁡θ,2sinh⁡ϕcos⁡θ⟩

where θ∈[0,2π) and ϕ∈R.

Therefore, the third component of f is 2sinh⁡ϕcos⁡θ.
